title: Go-to-Prod: Equity & Risk Alignment Checklist
summary: Working checklist and KPI tracker for final go/no-go alignment focused on customer equity, operational risk, and capacity plan for product launches. Intended as a cross-functional artifact to unify legal, security, product, and ops signoffs.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight go-to-prod checklist that centers equity and risk considerations into the final gating decisions. It complements the existing launch runbooks by explicitly calling out differential user impact, rollback thresholds tied to quality/KPIs, and cross-team owners for mitigations.

Scope:
- Applies to feature launches and model rollouts with public exposure or customer-facing behaviors (hosted API, dedicated customers, and private deployments).
- Focus areas: fairness/regression risk, privacy & data handling, capacity & latency SLOs, incident playbooks, comms & escalation.

Definitions / Quick glossary:
- Differential Impact: measurable differences in product outputs or performance across customer cohorts (region, language, account size, accessibility needs).
- Equity KPI: a metric that tracks parity across cohorts (e.g., median-latency delta, top-5 failure-rate by cohort, qualitative harm flags).
- Risk Threshold: pre-agreed limit that triggers rollback or throttling (e.g., >2x error rate for any cohort, SLA breach >10% below target for 15m).

Checklist (pre-launch alignment):
[ ] Product owner has defined 3 primary KPIs (latency, error rate, qualitative quality) and baseline values for current cohort distributions.
[ ] Equity KPIs defined and instrumented (examples below). Owner: Product-ops / Research-ML.
[ ] Risk thresholds and automatic mitigations documented (circuit-breakers, auto-fallback to previous model). Owner: SRE / Serving-runtime.
[ ] Privacy & data handling signoff (PII flows, logging retention, opt-out) from Security & Compliance. Owner: Security.
[ ] Legal and policy review completed for regulated markets (EU, UK, CA health-related verticals). Owner: Legal.
[ ] Customer Success and Solutions Engineering have run smoke tests for top 5 enterprise customers (if applicable). Owner: Solutions-eng.
[ ] Communication templates prepared for internal ops, affected customers, and public incident pages. Owner: comms/product.

Equity KPI Examples (instrumentation required pre-launch):
- Latency parity: 95th percentile latency per region/language (alert if any cohort > baseline * 1.5).
- Error parity: proportion of API calls flagged as failing or low-confidence by cohort (alert if delta > 3 percentage points).
- Quality parity: top-line quality score on curated prompt sets per demographic segment (automated A/B evals).
- Accessibility checks: number of failures in accessibility prompts / assistive tech scenarios.
- Customer impact score: aggregated SLO breach * revenue weighting (helps prioritize rollbacks).

Operational KPIs and thresholds (suggested starter values):
- Global 95p latency <= baseline + 20% (soft), >40% (hard).
- Error rate <= baseline + 1.5 percentage points (soft), >3pp (hard).
- Equity parity delta <= 2pp for primary cohorts (soft), >4pp (hard).
- Infra CPU/GPU utilization below commit: keep sustained utilization <75% for 30m; >90% sustained triggers scale-up/traffic-shift.

Rollout gating and actions (decision matrix):
- If soft threshold violated for <30m: notify on-call, raise priority ticket, enable canary throttling to 25% traffic and continue monitoring.
- If soft threshold sustained >30m or multiple cohorts impacted: pause further rollout, escalate to incident commander, run mitigation playbook.
- If hard threshold triggered: immediate rollback to previous model or traffic cutover to fallback cluster, notify customers per comms template.

Staffing & Capacity Tally (quick table to fill before launch):
- Primary on-call (prod-owner): __________________
- SRE responder: __________________
- Model/research lead: __________________
- Solutions/cs lead: __________________
- Legal/security advisor (on-call window): __________________
- Launch window staffing hours (local TZ): __________________
- Expected QPS baseline and peak (estimate): baseline = _____ QPS; peak = _____ QPS; committed capacity = _____ GPUs / pods
- Safety margin: recommended +30% headroom vs peak for first 48h

Communication and Customer Playbook Snippets:
- Internal: incident channel (slack #prod-incidents), on-call bridge link, abbreviated status cadence (T+15m, T+1h, T+4h).
- Customer: private notice for affected enterprise accounts if any equity or compliance concern detected; public postmortem if service or quality regression visible to >1% of active users.

Open questions & follow-ups (action items):
- [ ] Data team to provide cohort definitions and sampling plan for equity evals (owner: Rina Kumar, due: 2025-02-20)
- [ ] Research to deliver baseline A/B script and initial evaluation results (owner: Carlos Vega, due: 2025-02-24)
- [ ] SRE to add auto fallback circuit for model variant selection (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2025-02-28)
- [ ] Legal to confirm jurisdictional communications cadence for regulated markets (owner: Maya Lin, due: 2025-02-22)

Appendix: quick templates (paste into Confluence/issue)
- Incident subject line: [LAUNCH] <feature> - equity alert - cohort=<cohort> - KPI=<metric>
- Customer advisory opener: "We detected an anomaly in <feature> affecting a subset of requests in <region>. We're actively throttling traffic and working on a remediation. No customer data was exposed."

Notes / working assumptions (store experimental context here):
- Baselines are derived from last 30 days; if sample size for a cohort < 1k calls/day, use combined-week baseline and mark as high variance.
- Equity checks are prioritized by risk to user safety and revenue impact (order: safety, compliance, revenue).
- This checklist intentionally keeps mitigation options conservative for the first 72 hours post-launch. After that, the team can relax thresholds if signals are stable for 7 days.
